## About this page

Keeps this vault the same on your devices, and opens vaults held somewhere else, such as a KeePass file or a Bitwarden account.

#### How it works

There are two ways to sync this vault, and you can use both:

- [Your devices, on this network](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-lan): two devices talk directly, with nothing in between.
- [Through a folder or server](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-files): each device leaves its own encrypted copy at a place and merges the others.

Both merge field by field. If two devices changed the same value, the one that loses goes into that item's history, so a conflict never destroys a password.

[Accounts held elsewhere](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-accounts) are other vaults, which open at the door in place of this one. Further down are [nested and shared vaults](/guide/settings/vaults/), and [receiving one item](/guide/settings/receive/) from another device.

See also [Keeping devices in sync](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-sync), [Syncing over your own network](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-lan), [Backups](/guide/settings/backup/).

<a id="group-sync-account"></a>

## This account

The server account that is open now, and how its changes reach the server.

#### How it works

Changes go up after each edit. If the server cannot be reached, they wait on this device and go up on the next try.

**Sync now** takes your changes up and brings the server's changes down.

What travels is your items, encrypted the way any Bitwarden client encrypts them, to the server you signed in to.

#### Limits

Shown only while a Bitwarden, Vaultwarden or WM Pass server account is open.

See also [Accounts held elsewhere](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-accounts), [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

<a id="group-sync-lan"></a>

## Your devices, on this network

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Syncs this vault directly with a phone or another computer on the same network, with no server in between.

#### Why it is there

Nothing leaves your network, and there is no account to make or trust.

#### How it works

Pair each device once with [Pair a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-pair). Pairing stores the other device's key, and later connections with any other key are refused.

Paired devices sync on their own while both are on this network with the vault unlocked: a computer whenever its vault is open, a phone while WM Pass is on screen. Each looks for the others soon after unlocking, about 20 seconds after a change, and every five minutes. They send each other what differs, attachments included, and merge it field by field.

**Sync now** does the same at once. A phone that is closed or in the background is not waiting, so a computer catches up with it the next time it is open.

Each device's row says how its last sync went, so a failure shows beside the device it came from.

Being paired is not enough on its own. Before anything is sent, each side proves it holds this vault's key, so two devices with different vaults can pair but never sync. [Merge vaults](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-merge) makes them one.

Devices find each other with mDNS, under a random name that says nothing about you or the vault. Everything after that is encrypted end to end between the two.

Click a paired device to rename it, sync with it alone, merge vaults with it, or forget it. A name you give it stays on this computer. A forgotten device has to pair again before it can sync.

#### Limits

It counts as network use, so it needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

After you rekey the vault, the other device fails the check until it is unlocked with the new key.

The computer waits and syncs only while the vault is unlocked, and not for an account or a nested vault.

#### On Android

Start with [Add a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-add), which asks whether the other device already has this vault: one with none gets a copy, one that has it is paired. Pairing stores the other device's key, and later connections with any other key are refused.

Paired devices sync on their own while both are on this network with the vault unlocked: a computer whenever its vault is open, this phone while WM Pass is on screen. Each looks for the others when you unlock or come back to the app, about 20 seconds after a change, and every five minutes. **Sync now** does the same at once, and [Wait for one](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-wait) keeps this phone waiting on this page.

They send each other what differs, attachments included, and merge it field by field. Each device's row says how its last sync went, so a failure shows beside the device it came from.

Being paired is not enough on its own. Before anything is sent, each side proves it holds this vault's key, so two devices with different vaults can pair but never sync. [Merge vaults](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-merge) makes them one.

Devices find each other with mDNS, under a random name that says nothing about you or the vault. Everything after that is encrypted end to end between the two.

Tap a paired device to rename it, sync with it alone, merge vaults with it, or forget it. A name you give it stays on this phone. A forgotten device has to pair again before it can sync.

Android files this under internet access, so it needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed) like the rest.

After you rekey the vault, the other device fails the check until it is unlocked with the new key.

With **Wait for one**, keep the phone on this page until the sync is done. Leaving it stops the wait.

See also [Syncing over your own network](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-lan), [Pair a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-pair), [Wait for one](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-wait), [Merge vaults](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-merge).

<a id="action-lan-add"></a>

## Add a device

*Only in Android.*

Starts syncing this vault with another phone or computer on this Wi-Fi.

#### How it works

It first asks whether WM Pass on the other device already opens this vault.

- **No, it has no vault yet** sends it a copy of this one, then pairs the two. See [Add a new device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-join).
- **Yes, it has this vault**, from a backup or a sync folder, pairs the two so they can sync. See [Pair a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-pair).

#### Limits

Two vaults made separately stay separate: pairing does not merge them, and a paired device syncs only if it holds this vault's key. To make them one, use [Merge vaults](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-merge) once they are paired.

See also [Add a new device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-join), [Pair a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-pair), [Your devices, on this network](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-lan).

<a id="action-lan-pair"></a>

## Pair a device

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Introduces another device to this one, once, so the two can sync over this network.

#### How it works

Choose one of five ways. Each ends with both devices holding the other's key.

- With **Show a code**, this computer shows a QR code for the other device to scan, and the same code as text for a computer that cannot scan. It works once and stops in two minutes.
- With **Scan a code**, the other device shows its code, and this computer's camera reads it.
- With **Paste a code**, the other device shows its code, and you paste its text here.
- With **Compare six digits**, this side waits and the other connects. Both screens show six digits, and if they match you choose **They match** on both.
- **Compare six digits, finding the other** does the same from the side that connects to a device already waiting.

#### Limits

If the six digits differ, choose **They differ**, and nothing is stored.

Pairing alone opens nothing: a paired device must also hold this vault's key to sync.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Pair a device that has this vault.

Introduces a device that already opens this vault to this one, once, so the two can sync over this network. Reached from [Add a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-add).

Choose one of four ways. Each ends with both devices holding the other's key.

- With **Show a code**, this phone shows a QR code for the other device to scan. It works once and stops in two minutes.
- With **Scan a code**, the other device shows a code, and you scan it here.
- **Compare six digits** is for when a camera will not do. This side waits and the other connects. Both screens show six digits, and if they match you choose **They match** on both.
- **Compare six digits, finding the other** does the same from the side that connects to a device already waiting.

See also [Your devices, on this network](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-lan), [Wait for one](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-wait).

<a id="action-lan-join"></a>

## Add a new device

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Sends this vault to a phone or computer that has none yet, and pairs the two for syncing.

#### How it works

First, on the new device, choose **I already have a vault**, then Get it from another device. It shows a code and waits.

- **Scan its code** reads the QR code on the new device's screen with this computer's camera, or from a picture of it.
- **Find it on this network** looks for it, then both screens show six digits. If they match, choose **They match** on both.
- **Paste its code** takes the text under the new device's QR code, for a computer or the terminal app.

The new device then asks for this vault's master password.

#### Limits

It sends the vault you opened at the door, not an account or a nested vault.

If the six digits differ, choose **They differ**, and nothing is sent.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Send this vault to a new device.

Sends this vault to a phone or computer that has none yet, and pairs the two for syncing. Reached from [Add a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-add), choosing **No, it has no vault yet**.

First, on the new device, choose **I already have a vault**, then Get it from another device. It shows a code and waits.

- **Scan its code** reads the QR code on the new device's screen, from a computer, a phone or the terminal app.
- **Paste its code** takes the text under the code, for a computer or the terminal app.
- **Find it on this network** looks for it, then both screens show six digits. If they match, tap **They match** on both.

The new device then asks for this vault's master password.

See also [Pair a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-pair), [Your devices, on this network](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-lan).

<a id="action-lan-wait"></a>

## Wait for one

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Makes this device visible on the network and waits for a paired device to choose **Sync now** or ask to merge vaults.

#### How it works

One side waits, and the other spends a few seconds looking for a paired device that is waiting. When they are done, both say what was sent and received. **Stop** ends the wait. A request to merge vaults asks here before anything moves.

#### Limits

If **Sync now** on the other device finds nobody, check that both are on the same network and that this one is still waiting.

See also [Your devices, on this network](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-lan), [Pair a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-pair), [Merge vaults](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-merge).

<a id="action-lan-merge"></a>

## Merge vaults

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Makes two different vaults on two paired devices one vault. You choose which vault stays, and the other device's items move into it.

#### Why it is there

Two vaults made apart, even with the same items imported into both, have different keys and can never sync. A device row that says it has a different vault needs this once.

#### How it works

Open the paired device, choose **Merge vaults**, then which vault stays: this device's or the other's. On the other device, choose [Wait for one](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-wait) first; a computer with the vault open is already waiting.

The other device asks its person before anything moves, saying which vault stays.

The device that gives sends every item outside the trash, with attachments and folders, inside the encrypted connection. An item the kept vault already has, the same login for the same site with the same password, is merged field by field rather than doubled, so newer values win and older ones go to history.

The kept vault comes back to the giving device, which uses it in place of its own and deletes its old vault file. From then on you unlock it there with the kept vault's master password, and the two sync as usual.

#### When to use it

When a phone and a computer each had a vault of their own before they were paired.

#### Limits

The giving device's own vault file is gone afterwards, along with its settings and trash. Its items live on in the kept vault. Make a backup first if you want to keep that file as it was.

If the connection drops part way, the kept vault may already have the items, and the giving device keeps its own vault until the end. Run the merge again; items already there are matched, not doubled.

Both devices must be paired and on the same network, and it needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

See also [Your devices, on this network](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-lan), [Wait for one](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-wait), [Add a device](/guide/settings/sync/#action-lan-add).

<a id="group-sync-files"></a>

## Through a folder or server

Syncs this vault through any place you set up for backups. Each device leaves its own encrypted copy there and merges the others.

#### How it works

Turn on the switch beside a place to sync through it. **Add a place** sets up a new one, the same way as under [Backups](/guide/settings/backup/).

A sync runs about 20 seconds after your last change, so a burst of edits makes one trip. It also runs on its own, to bring in what your other devices changed: just after you unlock, when you come back to the window after a minute or more, and every five minutes while the vault is open. **Sync now** runs one at once.

Each device writes only its own file, so two devices syncing at the same moment cannot overwrite each other. A file that belongs to some other vault does not open and is left alone. Attachments go up once each and stay.

#### When to use it

When your devices are rarely on the same network, or you already use Syncthing, Nextcloud or a cloud drive.

#### Limits

It syncs the vault you opened at the door, only while it is unlocked, and not an account or a nested vault.

Any place but a folder needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

Sync is not a backup: a change on one device, moving an item to the trash included, reaches the others. Keep backups as well.

#### On Android

Turn on the switch beside a place to sync through it. Tap the place itself to change its details or stop using it. **Add a place** sets up a new one, the same way as under [Backups](/guide/settings/backup/).

A sync runs about 20 seconds after your last change, so a burst of edits makes one trip. It also runs on its own, to bring in what your other devices changed: just after you unlock, when you come back to the app after a minute or more, and every five minutes while the vault is open. **Sync now** runs one at once.

Each device writes only its own file, so two devices syncing at the same moment cannot overwrite each other. A file that belongs to some other vault does not open and is left alone. Attachments go up once each and stay.

See also [Keeping devices in sync](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-sync), [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place), [Backups](/guide/settings/backup/).

<a id="setting-sync-settings"></a>

## Sync settings with the vault

Keeps your customisations the same on every device that opens this vault: the look, the list, the editor, codes, the generator and the rest.

#### How it works

The settings travel inside the vault, encrypted with it, so every way the vault syncs carries them: your devices on this network, a folder or server, and a WM Pass server. A copy of the vault file says nothing about them.

Each setting goes on its own. When two devices change the same one, the later change wins on both.

The first device to sync brings what it has changed from the defaults. Turning this back on takes the settings the vault holds.

Keys for alias services and Have I Been Pwned are items in the vault, so they sync with it whether this is on or not.

#### Limits

Protection settings stay on each device: locking, the clipboard, screenshots, the network switch, and everything that lets another app or the browser in. So does what describes one window, such as its sidebar and the sections left open.

A setting one platform does not have is kept for the devices that do.

It follows the vault you opened at the door, not an account or a nested vault.

See also [Settings that stay on this device](/guide/settings/sync/#setting-sync-skip), [Through a folder or server](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-files), [Your devices, on this network](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-lan).

<a id="setting-sync-skip"></a>

## Settings that stay on this device

Settings this device neither sends to the vault nor takes from it. The others still sync.

#### How it works

Turn a setting off here when you want it different on this device, such as a bigger code size on the phone. Turning it back on takes the value the vault holds.

See also [Sync settings with the vault](/guide/settings/sync/#setting-sync-settings).

<a id="group-sync-accounts"></a>

## Accounts held elsewhere

Vaults that live somewhere other than this device: a KeePass file where it is, or an account on Bitwarden, Vaultwarden or a WM Pass server. Each one appears on the door beside this vault.

#### How it works

Adding one stores only where it is. You sign in at the door, where it opens in place of this vault.

A KeePass file stays where it is, and WM Pass writes back to it on each save. It keeps one earlier copy beside its own files, in case a write is cut off.

A server account keeps an offline copy here, encrypted as the server's is, so it opens without the network and catches up when it can.

The delete button beside an account removes it. WM Pass forgets it on this device, with its offline copy. Nothing on the server or in the file changes.

#### Limits

Bitwarden does not publish its API, so a change on their side can break this.

See also [Add an account](/guide/settings/sync/#action-add-account), [This account](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-account), [Unlock screen](/guide/screens/#screen-door).

<a id="action-add-account"></a>

## Add an account

Adds a KeePass file or a server account to the door. The delete button beside it in the list removes it again.

#### How it works

Signing in to a server sends your email address, a name and an id for this device, and a key derived from your password that proves who you are, as any Bitwarden client does. Your password itself is never sent. After that, your items travel encrypted.

Once it is added, **Sign in now** locks this vault and takes you to the door with the account chosen. **Later** leaves it there for next time.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Bitwarden | An account at bitwarden.com. |
| Bitwarden EU | An account at bitwarden.eu. |
| Own server | Vaultwarden, or the WM Pass server, at the address you type. |
| KeePass file | A .kdbx file, opened where it is. Syncthing or a cloud app can carry it between devices. |

#### Limits

Adding a server account turns on [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

Nothing is checked when you add it. Whether the address, email and password are right shows at the first sign-in, at the door.

WM Pass refuses a server that asks for weaker password protection than it accepts.

The first sign-in from a new device can be held back until you confirm it: Bitwarden emails a code, and the door asks for it beside your password.

#### On Android

Adds a KeePass file or a server account to the door. Tap one in the list to open it, change its details or remove it.

Signing in to a server sends your email address, a name and an id for this phone, and a key derived from your password that proves who you are, as any Bitwarden client does. Your password itself is never sent. After that, your items travel encrypted.

Once it is added, **Sign in now** locks this vault and takes you to the door with the account chosen. **Later** leaves it there for next time.

Adding a server account turns on [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

Before a server account is added, WM Pass checks that the address answers as a Bitwarden server does. Whether the email and password are right shows only at the first sign-in; until then the door offers **Change the details** and **Remove this account** when it fails.

WM Pass refuses a server that asks for weaker password protection than it accepts.

The first sign-in from a new device can be held back until you confirm it: Bitwarden emails a code, and the door asks for it beside your password.

See also [Accounts held elsewhere](/guide/settings/sync/#group-sync-accounts), [Unlock screen](/guide/screens/#screen-door).
